what_only_the_door_shows.limit: a structured argument cannot be held to a pattern at all, so an email's attachments - a list of objects - are outside what pinning reaches, whatever the operator knows about them
what_only_the_door_shows.refusal_says: only a text, a number, a Bool or a list of those
what_only_the_door_shows.shown_by: the workspace suite's user_task_33 attaches a file

arguments.title: Booking a room at the Riverside View Hotel

what_only_the_door_shows.limit: an argument held to a pattern has to be there, so a pin on an argument the task always passes also refuses a call that leaves it out - which is how several attacks are refused, and worth saying out loud rather than counting quietly
what_only_the_door_shows.refusal_says: held to a pattern and was not given
what_only_the_door_shows.shown_by: the travel suite's injection_task_2 creates an event with no location, where the user task names one

what_the_pattern_grammar_cannot_say.limit: a star never stands for white space, so no pattern matches a free-text argument of more than one word - not even '*'
and so no 'contains' pattern works on one either: the star would have to cross the spaces around the words it keeps
what_the_pattern_grammar_cannot_say.shown_by: '*meeting room*' against the slack suite's user_task_8 reply
what_the_pattern_grammar_cannot_say.value: I've seen it in the meeting room!

what_the_pattern_grammar_cannot_say.limit: a pattern is a whole-value match with no negation, so the useful pin for a message body - 'no address in it' - cannot be written at all
what_the_pattern_grammar_cannot_say.shown_by: no grammar for it; the nearest, a literal, holds the body to one exact string

what_the_pattern_grammar_cannot_say.limit: a number is held to the pattern its JSON text makes, so a pin written the way the task writes the amount does not match the number the door sees
what_the_pattern_grammar_cannot_say.shown_by: the banking suite's user_task_15 says 'refund that 10.00', and the door sees 10.0

what_the_pattern_grammar_cannot_say.limit: a star does stand for a digit, so a whole class of amounts can be pinned loosely - which is the wrong shape for money, where the useful bound is a maximum and there is no grammar for one
